world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. 2011. Linguistic Survey of India: Rajasthan (Part I).
sources.note: Kathodi named once in a list of tribal languages; no sketch.

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. 2003. Linguistic Survey of India: Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
sources.note: Kathodi appears only in tribe / mother-tongue tables (0.34% of population); no grammatical sketch of Kathodi in this volume.

Confirms that the only prior linguistic work on the dialect is Abbott 1905 and Grierson LSI VII/IX-III; other entries are ethnographic (Bombay Gazetteer, Enthoven, Weling 'The Katkaris', Karve & Dandekar) or general linguistics.

sources.citation: Kulkarni, S. B. 1969. Descriptive analysis of Kātkarī dialect. Ph.D. thesis (guide A. M. Ghatage), University of Poona / Deccan College Postgraduate and Research Institute, Poona. vii+696 pp. [Shodhganga handle 10603/160307]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Silent on stress. Ch. I Phonology (pp. 36-148) covers segmental phonemes, vowel length (not phonemic, p. 40), nasalisation (phonemic supra-segmental, pp. 40-43), aspiration, clusters, phoneme frequency, syllable system (pp. 137-148). No stress/accent subsection; 'stress' appears once (p. 68) only as a class name in the aspiration discussion. The introduction (p. 21) says 'More work needs to be done, especially with regard to suprasegmental features in phonology, and syntax.' Closest phonetic-prominence remark, p. 40: vowels of monosyllables are uniformly long, final-syllable vowels of polysyl…

sources.citation: Abbott, Justin E. 1905. The Kātkari Language (A Preliminary Study). Journal of the Bombay Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society, Centenary Memorial Volume (extra number), 78-127.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction, affinity with Marathi/Gujarati, a 'very incomplete' tentative grammar (nouns, pronouns, adjectives, adverbs, verbs), folklore/poetry, vocabulary in Devanagari. No pronunciation section; no occurrence of 'accent' or 'stress' in the article's scanned. Glottolog's journal title ('Royal Anthropological Society') is a garble of 'Royal Asiatic Society'.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX pt. III: The Bhil languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c.
sources.note: Kathodi only mentioned in passing (Surat/Navsari lists) and referred back to Vol. VII; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page katk1238 and reference records 85916 (Abbott 1905) and 550138 (Kulkarni 1969); Wikipedia 'Katkari language'
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; Glottolog lists only Abbott 1905, Kulkarni 1969 and Southworth 1976 (classification) for the language; Wikipedia is a stub citing Ethnologue only.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1905. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. VII: Indo-Aryan family, Southern group, Specimens of the Marathi language. Calcutta. Section 'Kāthoḍī or Kāṭkarī', pp. 130-140.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; classification remarks, genitive suffix, verb substantive, and three specimens (Thana, Kolaba, Janjira).

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. Linguistic Survey of India: Maharashtra / Gujarat volumes (in preparation or published after 2011), if they include a Kathodi/Katkari sketch
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The new Census LSI state volumes give short phonological sketches of scheduled-tribe languages, occasionally with a stress line; the Dadra & Nagar Haveli (2003) and Rajasthan (2011) volumes checked here have no Kathodi sketch; Maharashtra and Gujarat volumes were not found on archive.org.

sources.citation: Any field phonetic/phonological study of Katkari (Kathodi) word prosody — none is known to exist; Kulkarni 1969 (p. 21) states suprasegmentals were left for future work and no later description was found in Glottolog, Crossref, OpenAlex, Shodhganga, archive.org or Google Books.

sources.note: Would be the first statement of Katkari stress; the language has ~12,000 speakers (Ethnologue 2007) and only one full description (1969) which is silent on stress.
